reason: The image-only reading did not see the typed slip and read only scattered words on the upside-down face; the reread on rotated native crops gives the sellers, Ögsten, St. Petersberg, Chiemsee and St Genevieve's day, and identifies Ögsten as Östen in Umhausen, not Oetz.
sources: Die Gemeindearchive des Bezirkes Imst (Tiroler Landesarchiv, 1995), Umhausen: 'Hanns Viechrueter von Östen (Ögsten) im Ötztal ... Baurechte auf chiemseeische Lehen' (Google Books, snippet)
Tiroler Familiennamenkunde (1990): Frauenchiemsee's rent register of 1400 spells Östen (Ötztal) 'Awsten' (Google Books, snippet)
Typed partial transcription and pencil notes on the paper slip photographed with the fragment (canvas 0, Stams_STA_Frg_048_01r_Adl_01r), compared, not independent
text:
Source-assisted reading (research reader, Claude), reread on the native image rotated 180 degrees: the text face (canvas 1, Stams_STA_Frg_048_01v_Adl_01v, 4912 x 7360, photographed upside down) in a grid of crops (rotated view x 250-4700, y 1150-4410), with enhanced detail crops of the opening lines, the object, the landlord line and the dating clause. Read before comparison with the typed slip and pencil notes on canvas 0. The central band is badly rubbed and was not read; the middle of every line is lost in the cut slot; the lower-left corner is chamfered. A blind word check on neutral crops was inconclusive on the faded text. Boxes are native pixels of the unrotated image. Expansions in parentheses, uncertain readings (?), losses [...].
